title: Character count
overview: A live count (or word count) when a length limit is justified.
apply_when: A justified max length on a field.
not_when: An unjustified limit, or a closed choice dumped into a textarea (use radio).

vs.why: the field; this is the count accessory

role.overview: A live count for a field that has a limit.
role.apply_when: A textarea or text field with a maximum.
role.not_when: A limit with no visible count, or a count with no field.

size.overview: Highest in the size hierarchy — the easiest to hit.
size.apply_when: The view's main instance, or full-width on a small viewport.
size.not_when: A dense toolbar or a third option next to the main control.

size.apply_when: Ordinary use in forms, pages, and chrome.
size.not_when: The only control on a mobile screen that should span the width.

size.overview: Lowest in the size hierarchy — densest.
size.apply_when: Inline or chrome that sits beside content.
size.not_when: The page's primary instance, or a control under 44×44.

composition.overview: The count sits with the field it describes.

state.overview: Under the limit. The count is available to AT.
Over the limit. The field is in error and the count says so.
state.not_when: A red count with no field error.

accessibility.overview: The count is tied to the field.
accessibility.not_when: A floating number with no aria-describedby.

accessibility.overview: Crossing the limit is announced without stealing focus.
accessibility.apply_when: They go over or back under.

keyboard.overview: Tab lands on the field, not a separate count control.
keyboard.not_when: The count is a fake tab stop.
